Senses.Explanation: To discuss or deliberate is to work something over in speech or thought, alone or with another person. Nanquan says that he and Guizong have discussed phrases together and invites a capable participant to come out and discuss; Fengxue asks whether discussion belongs in the quarters or tea hall. Other speakers turn the same act into a warning. Dahui forbids reckless deliberation after the Second Patriarch’s bow and catalogues “needle-and-thread” discussions of an old case; Sanyi Mingyu rejects making Buddhist analysis of a rain display. Baoen Yuan says even “nothing-to-do discussion” is grit in the eye, while a verse speaks of ages spent deliberating. Zen does not give the word one stance: public consultation and the criticized working-over of cases are attested uses of the same act.

Senses.Explanation: “The Old Woman Burns the Hermitage” names the whole encounter among the old woman, the young woman, and the hermitage-dweller, not only its final fire. In its repeated narrative, an old woman supports a hermitage-dweller for twenty years and sends a young woman to attend him. The young woman embraces him and asks, ‘at just such a time, how is it?’ He answers, ‘a withered tree leans against a cold cliff; through the three winter months there is no warmth.’ On hearing the report, the old woman says that for twenty years she has supported only a common fellow, drives him out, and burns the hermitage. Later masters cite, verse, question, and re-appraise the case: one asks why various quarters support the recorded questioner; another proposes that the hermitage-dweller should have laughed when approached; another says that to uphold the school and establish the teaching requires such a person, speaking of the old woman. These opposed recorded appraisals belong to the case's reception; this entry does not decide between them.
